features.method: Convex hull, computed in the UTM plane, of the 1587 stations that sdMap.csv flags sd1500 = 1 and that the release marks as still operating (31 hull vertices), converted to latitude and longitude. Earlier version of this record used every station ever flagged (1640 rows, 32 vertices, 3158 km2); stations that have since stopped are now left out. Station positions are the northing and easting columns of sdMap.csv in the Pierre Auger Collaboration Open Data release 3 (20 March 2024, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10488964), which the Collaboration describes as "UTC" [sic] coordinates in metres (the data page does not state the zone or datum). They are read as UTM zone 19 south (central meridian 69 deg W) on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (EPSG:32719) because only zone 19 puts the numbers at Malargue (the converted stations span latitude 34.93 to 35.52 S and longitude 68.91 to 69.66 W), and WGS 84 is the GPS datum; this reading is this work's assumption, hence confidence approximate and accuracy_m 50. The hull is a computed outline, not a published boundary, and a convex hull slightly over-states a concave array.
features.name: Pierre Auger Observatory surface-detector array (1500 m spacing), convex hull of active stations

provenance.locator: sdMap.csv (release 3), rows with sd1500 = 1 and stop = 1 (1587 of 1689 rows); hull computed in the UTM plane then converted
provenance.note: Confidence derived: the vertices are published station positions, the hull and the UTM 19S/WGS 84 reading are this work.

features.method: Convex hull of the 71 stations flagged sd750=1 in the Auger open-data station table sdMap.csv (49 sd750-only plus 22 flagged both sd1500 and sd750), using the same UTM-to-WGS84 conversion and hull algorithm as the Auger SD-1500 array boundary. The computed area is 29.3 km^2, 24.7% above the 23.5 km^2 quoted for the '61-detector infilled array' in a collaboration publication. The 71-station sd750 flag count also does not match the quoted 61 detectors, so the flag very likely uses a looser definition of 'infill station' than the one behind the quoted figure. For that reason no check against the quoted area is asserted.
features.name: Pierre Auger Observatory infill surface-detector array (750 m spacing), convex hull

provenance.locator: sdMap.csv, rows with sd750=1 (71 of 1690)

summary.plain: The Pierre Auger Observatory's array of about 1,600 water-filled detector tanks on the Pampa Amarilla near Malargue, Argentina, with every working station drawn at its surveyed position, plus the outline of the main array and of the denser infill. The four fluorescence telescope sites are not drawn.
